example.en: I like it a lot; the color is perfect.
I love it; where did you get it?
I'm into hiking these days.

entries.head: I'm a big fan of something

example.en: I'm a big fan of that band.
example.zh: 我是那个乐队的大粉丝。

example.en: It was love at first sight for them.
The song grows on you after a few listens.
example.zh: 这首歌听几遍就渐渐喜欢上了。

example.en: I can't get enough of this show.
I'm crazy about spicy food.
Cheap, fast and close—what's not to love?
example.zh: 便宜、快、又近，怎么会不喜欢？

example.en: A cold beer after work really hits the spot.
example.zh: 下班后一杯冰啤酒正合我意。

example.en: I can't stand the noise from upstairs.
Horror movies are not my cup of tea.
I hate it when the app logs me out.
example.zh: 我讨厌 App 把我登出。

example.en: The endless meetings give me a headache.
example.zh: 没完没了的会让我头疼。

example.en: The dripping faucet drives me up the wall.
example.zh: 滴水的水龙头吵得我受不了。

example.en: I can do without the drama.
Camping is not my thing.
I'd rather not talk about it.
The new design leaves me cold.
I'm sick of the same lunch every day.
example.zh: 我烦透了每天一样的午饭。

example.en: No way! You got the job?
example.zh: 不可能吧！你拿到工作了？

example.en: Is that so? I didn't know that.
I can't believe it; the tickets sold out.
My goodness, look at the size of that fish.
example.zh: 我的天哪，看那条鱼多大。

example.en: What a surprise; I didn't expect you here.
example.zh: 真是个惊喜，没想到你在这儿。

example.en: Guess what? We got the funding.
example.zh: 你猜怎么着？我们拿到资金了。

example.en: Are you serious? The flight is canceled?
example.zh: 你是认真的吗？航班取消了？

example.en: The view from the top blew my mind.
That's incredible; she finished in two hours.
example.zh: 太不可思议了，她两小时就做完了。

example.en: For real? You met the director?
I'm so happy you could come.

variants.head: thrilled

example.en: They were thrilled when the offer came through.
example.zh: offer 下来时他们特别高兴。

variants.note_zh: 比 happy 更强调因好消息而高兴；人和自己都能说。

variants.head: ecstatic

example.en: He was ecstatic when his team won.
example.zh: 他的队赢了，他欣喜若狂。

variants.note_zh: 程度最重，高兴到失控；比 thrilled 更夸张。

variants.head: in high spirits

example.en: She's been in high spirits all week.

variants.note_zh: 偏整体状态好、外显；不是某一件事带来的高兴。

example.en: That's great news; congratulations!
I'm thrilled about the new apartment.
I'm in a great mood today.
Your message really made my day.
example.zh: 你的消息让我开心了一整天。

example.en: I'm so excited about the trip.
example.zh: 这次旅行让我太激动了。

variants.head: pumped

example.en: I'm pumped for the concert.
example.zh: 演唱会让我兴奋得不行。

variants.note_zh: 带一股冲劲，多为自己期待的事；比 excited 更口语。

variants.head: stoked

example.en: We're stoked about the trip.

variants.note_zh: 比 pumped 更随意、更年轻；常和 about 连用。

variants.head: can't wait

example.en: I can't wait to try that new place.
example.zh: 我等不及去试那家新店。

variants.note_zh: 最常用，直接说期待；后面接 to do。

example.en: I'm in a good mood because it's Friday.
What a wonderful day for a picnic.
example.zh: 多美好的一天，适合野餐。

example.en: She smiled from ear to ear when she saw the gift.
example.zh: 看到礼物她笑得合不拢嘴。

entries.head: this is the best day ever

example.en: This is the best day ever!
I'm sad that you're leaving.

variants.head: down

example.en: I've been feeling down since the layoffs.
example.zh: 裁员以后我一直情绪低落。

variants.note_zh: 口语，比 sad 轻；常指一阵子的低落。

variants.head: heartbroken

example.en: She was heartbroken after the breakup.

variants.note_zh: 程度最重，多指感情或失去亲人；不是一般难过。

variants.head: blue

example.en: He's been a bit blue lately.

variants.note_zh: 轻度忧郁，偏文学/口语；不是“蓝色”。

example.en: I'm so upset about the result.
It breaks my heart to see the old street gone.
example.zh: 看到老街没了，我很心碎。

example.en: I miss my grandma a lot.
I've been feeling low since the move.
example.zh: 搬过来以后我一直情绪低落。

example.en: He's having a hard time at work.
example.zh: 他工作上的日子不好过。

example.en: She held back tears during the meeting.
I want to cry every time I hear that song.
example.zh: 每次听到那首歌我都想哭。

example.en: He's been down in the mouth all week.
I'm feeling blue today; it's raining.
example.zh: 今天下雨，我心情有点忧郁。

example.en: I'm so angry I can't think straight.
example.zh: 我气坏了，脑子都不转了。

variants.head: furious

example.en: She was furious about the canceled flight.

variants.note_zh: 比 angry 重，明显发火；正式和口语都能用。

variants.head: livid

example.en: He was livid when he saw the bill.

variants.note_zh: 口语，极度生气；不是“发青”。

variants.head: steaming

example.en: She was still steaming about it the next day.
example.zh: 第二天她还在为这事生气。

variants.note_zh: 气还没消、憋着一股火；比 angry 更形象。

example.en: I'm mad at my brother for borrowing my car.
example.zh: 我生我哥的气，他借我车。

example.en: That's the last straw; I'm calling the manager.
example.zh: 我再也忍不了了，我要找经理。

example.en: I've had it with these delays.
I can't take it anymore; the noise never stops.
example.zh: 我再也受不了了，噪音没停过。

example.en: I see red when someone cuts in line.
example.zh: 有人插队我就火冒三丈。

example.en: Watch your mouth; that's my friend.
example.zh: 注意你的言辞，那是我朋友。

example.en: I'm fuming; they canceled at the last minute.
example.zh: 我气炸了，他们最后一刻取消。

example.en: Leave me alone; I need a minute.
That is so unfair; I did most of the work.
example.zh: 太不公平了，大部分活是我干的。

example.en: I'm worried about the interview tomorrow.

variants.head: concerned

example.en: I'm concerned about the delay.

variants.note_zh: 比 worried 正式，偏理性关注；常用于工作。

variants.head: uneasy

example.en: I felt uneasy about the offer.
example.zh: 这个报价让我有点不安。

variants.note_zh: 说不出哪里不对的不安；比 worried 轻。

variants.head: stressing

example.en: I've been stressing about the exam.
example.zh: 考试的事我一直很焦虑。

variants.note_zh: 口语，常和 about 连用；比 worried 更强调压力。

example.en: What if the train is late?
I can't relax until I know the result.
example.zh: 知道结果之前我放松不下来。

example.en: I get butterflies in my stomach before every presentation.
example.zh: 每次演讲前我都紧张得心怦怦跳。

example.en: The deadline keeps me up at night.
example.zh: 截止日期让我夜不能寐。

example.en: What's wrong? You look worried.
Something bothers me about that email.
example.zh: 那封邮件有件事让我不安。

example.en: I have a bad feeling about this.
The rent increase is on my mind.
example.zh: 涨房租的事我一直惦记着。

example.en: We'll hope for the best and plan for the worst.
I'm afraid of heights.
You scared me; I didn't hear you come in.
example.zh: 你吓死我了，没听见你进来。

example.en: She was shaking like a leaf after the accident.
example.zh: 事故后她抖得像片叶子。

example.en: The scream made my blood run cold.
example.zh: 那声尖叫吓得我血都凉了。

example.en: I jumped out of my skin when the alarm went off.
example.zh: 闹钟响的时候我吓了一大跳。

example.en: My heart was in my mouth during the landing.
example.zh: 降落时我心提到嗓子眼。

example.en: Hold your breath and count to ten.
The only way is to face your fears.
example.zh: 唯一的办法是直面恐惧。

example.en: I was scared to death in that elevator.
example.zh: 在那部电梯里我吓得要死。

example.en: The dog froze in fear when the door slammed.
example.zh: 门砰地关上，狗吓得僵住了。

example.en: I'm tired; let's call it a night.
I'm worn out from the move.
I'm ready for bed; good night.
I'm beat; can we talk tomorrow?
I can barely stay awake in this meeting.
example.zh: 这个会我困得睁不开眼。

example.en: I need a nap before dinner.
I've been running on empty all week.
It's been a long day; I'm going to bed.
I need to catch up on sleep this weekend.
I'm bored; let's do something.

variants.head: restless

example.en: The kids get restless on long car rides.
example.zh: 长途车上孩子们坐不住。

variants.note_zh: 身体上想动、静不下来；比 bored 更强调躁动。

variants.head: stir-crazy

example.en: I'm going stir-crazy at home.

variants.note_zh: 长时间待在一个地方闷坏了；口语，常和 go 连用。

variants.head: over it

example.en: I'm so over this show.

variants.note_zh: 口语，已经腻了、不想再碰；比 bored 更带态度。

example.en: There's nothing to do in this town.
It's so boring; I want to leave.
We played cards to kill time.
There's nothing on TV tonight.
Work is the same old same old.
What should we do? I'm bored.
example.zh: 我们该做什么？我很无聊。

example.en: I can't sit still in long meetings.
This class never ends.
Sitting at home alone is no fun.
example.zh: 一个人待在家里没意思。

example.en: I can't wait for the weekend.
This is so cool; look at the lights.
Bring it on; I'm ready.
example.zh: 放马过来吧，我准备好了。

example.en: Here we go; the show is starting.
She's counting down the days to the trip.
I felt on top of the world after the offer.
example.zh: 拿到 offer 后我欣喜若狂。

example.en: My heart is full seeing everyone here.
example.zh: 看到大家都在，我心里满满的。

example.en: The kids jumped for joy when it snowed.
example.zh: 下雪时孩子们高兴得跳起来。

example.en: The big day is here; let's go.

entries.head: I am so ready for this

example.en: I am so ready for this.
I am so disappointed with the service.

variants.head: let down

example.en: I felt let down by the result.

variants.note_zh: 被人或结果辜负；常和 feel 连用。

variants.head: devastated

example.en: He was devastated by the news.
example.zh: 这个消息让他深受打击。

variants.note_zh: 程度重，多指坏消息；比 disappointed 强得多。

variants.head: crushed

example.en: She was crushed when she didn't get in.

variants.note_zh: 希望落空后的难过；比 disappointed 更重、更口语。

example.en: I don't want to let the team down.
The offer was too good to be true.
example.zh: 那个报价好得不像真的。

example.en: Don't get your hopes up; it's not confirmed.
What a waste of time.
So much for the picnic; it's raining.
It didn't work out; we're still friends.
Not my lucky day; I left my keys inside.
example.zh: 今天不走运，钥匙锁屋里了。

entries.head: I had my heart set on something

example.en: I had my heart set on that apartment.
All that work for nothing.
Give it your all and don't look back.
Keep it up; you're improving fast.
Stick with it; it gets easier.
example.zh: 坚持下去，会越来越轻松。

example.en: Go for it; you have nothing to lose.
example.zh: 大胆去做，你没什么可失去的。

example.en: Believe in yourself; you're ready.
Stay strong; the treatment is almost over.
Take a chance and apply for the job.
example.zh: 大胆试一试，去申请这份工作。

example.en: Almost there; just one more mile.

entries.head: you are on the right track

example.en: You are on the right track; keep going.
It's all right; accidents happen.
Don't worry; we'll figure it out.
Everything will be all right; you'll see.
example.zh: 一切都会好的，你会看到的。

example.en: Don't blame yourself; it could happen to anyone.
It's not your fault; the file was corrupted.
Give her a hug; she's had a rough day.

entries.head: it is not the end of the world

example.en: It's not the end of the world; try again.
Let it all out; I'm here.
You are not alone; we're all here.
I'm scared of speaking in front of a big crowd.
example.zh: 我害怕在很多人面前讲话。

variants.head: freaked out

example.en: I freaked out when the elevator stopped.

variants.note_zh: 一时的惊慌反应，比 scared 更口语；可以说人也可以说事。

variants.head: terrified

example.en: She's terrified of flying.

variants.note_zh: 程度最重，接近“恐惧”；可指长期害怕某件事。

variants.head: spooked

example.en: The dog got spooked by the thunder.

variants.note_zh: 被突然的事吓一跳，常指动物；比 scared 更轻、更口语。

example.en: I'm annoyed by the noise from upstairs.

variants.head: irritated

example.en: I'm irritated by the constant notifications.
example.zh: 没完没了的通知让我很烦。

variants.note_zh: 比 annoyed 正式一点，程度也轻；多指反复的小事。

variants.head: ticked off

example.en: He was ticked off about the late delivery.

variants.note_zh: 美式口语，明显生气；比 annoyed 重，但不到 furious。

variants.head: fed up

example.en: I'm fed up with these delays.

variants.note_zh: 长期积累的厌烦，不是一时烦；常和 with 连用。

example.en: I was embarrassed when I forgot her name.
example.zh: 忘了她名字时我很尴尬。

variants.head: mortified

example.en: I was mortified when I called him by the wrong name.
example.zh: 我叫错他名字时尴尬死了。

variants.note_zh: 程度最重，尴尬到想找地缝；偏书面但口语也用。

variants.head: awkward

example.en: It was awkward when nobody spoke.

variants.note_zh: 多指场面或气氛尴尬，不一定怪自己；也可说人。

variants.head: red-faced

example.en: He was red-faced after tripping on stage.
example.zh: 他在台上绊了一下，脸都红了。

variants.note_zh: 外在表现，脸红了；比 embarrassed 更具体、更口语。

example.en: I was surprised to see him at the party.
example.zh: 在聚会上看到他我很惊讶。

variants.head: shocked

example.en: I was shocked to hear the store is closing.
example.zh: 听说店要关门我很震惊。

variants.note_zh: 比 surprised 重，多指坏消息或意外大事。

variants.head: taken aback

example.en: She was taken aback by the question.

variants.note_zh: 被突然的话或举动弄得一愣，偏书面；程度比 shocked 轻。

variants.head: stunned

example.en: We were stunned by the result.

variants.note_zh: 惊得说不出话，程度重；可以是被好事也可以是被坏事。

example.en: I'm confused about which form to fill out.

variants.head: lost

example.en: I'm lost; can you start again?

variants.note_zh: 口语，指完全跟不上解释；比 confused 更强调“听晕了”。

variants.head: mixed up

example.en: I mixed up the two dates.

variants.note_zh: 把东西或概念弄混，不是听不懂；常和 the two 连用。

variants.head: puzzled

example.en: She looked puzzled by the instructions.

variants.note_zh: 纳闷、想不通，程度比 confused 轻；偏中性。

example.en: I felt lonely during my first month in the city.
example.zh: 刚来这座城市的第一个月我很孤独。

variants.head: isolated

example.en: Working from home can leave you isolated.
example.zh: 在家办公可能让人变得孤立。

variants.note_zh: 偏客观、长期，强调和外界断了联系；不一定是情绪上的孤独。

variants.head: left out

example.en: I felt left out when they made plans without me.
example.zh: 他们没叫我一起计划，我觉得被落下了。

variants.note_zh: 多指群体活动没被叫上，和 lonely 的“一个人”不同。

variants.head: on my own

example.en: I spent the holiday on my own.
example.zh: 这个假期我一个人过的。

variants.note_zh: 只是独自一人，不一定难过；lonely 才强调孤独感。

example.en: I'm grateful for everything you did.

variants.head: thankful

example.en: I'm thankful for your help.

variants.note_zh: 常对结果表示庆幸/感激，比 grateful 更轻；口语常用。

variants.head: appreciative

example.en: We're appreciative of the extra time.

variants.note_zh: 偏正式，多用于书面或公开场合；语气比 thankful 客气。

variants.head: indebted

example.en: I'm indebted to her for the referral.
example.zh: 她帮我内推，我欠她人情。

variants.note_zh: 正式，强调欠了人情/恩情；日常口语少用。

example.en: I'm proud of my team.

variants.head: pleased

example.en: I'm pleased with how it turned out.

variants.note_zh: 程度比 proud 轻，偏满意；正式和口语都能用。

variants.head: thrilled

example.en: We're thrilled for you.

variants.note_zh: 为好消息高兴，不强调“自豪”；比 pleased 重。

variants.head: beaming

example.en: Her parents were beaming at the ceremony.
example.zh: 典礼上她父母满脸笑意。

variants.note_zh: 外在表现，笑得合不拢嘴；比 proud 更具体。
